newsitem.title: USA: Champion says cautiously optimistic on Q2.
newsitem.headline: Champion says cautiously optimistic on Q2.

text.p: Champion International said it is "cautiously optimistic" for the second quarter because of its recently announced price increases for some products.

"We have recently announced price increases for certain grades of uncoated freesheet and coated groundwood papers, newsprint and pulp. As a result, we are cautiously optimistic that we will see some improvement in the second quarter," said chief executive Richard Olsen.

"Our paper and wood products manufacturing facilities are running well. Across the company, production was up and costs were down in the first quarter. Our employees are really focusing on reducing spending. Their collective efforts are beginning to be reflected in our operating results," he said.
The company reported a first quarter loss of $0.39 per share compared with a profit of $0.88 a share a year earlier.
Champion said Friday its first quarter losses reflect lower pulp and paper prices, which more than offset a strong performance by the wood products segment.
The company said the pulp and paper price decline was due principally to lower prices for uncoated free sheet and coated groundwood papers and pulp.
